units: Document defines defeat conditions for the benchmark, Adaptive Inheritance hypothesis, and measurement framework.
Central falsifiable claim is E* -> at least one invalidated authority weight decreases.
ARR is invalid if ARR≈0 while the supposedly invalid mechanism continues controlling future behavior.
Structural-distance operator fails if cosmetic changes exceed threshold or genuinely different mechanisms fall below threshold.
RAHU-0 fails if pure noise systematically causes structural updates or true structural failure is systematically classified as noise.
RAHU-1 is challenged if local patching remains indefinitely effective without complexity growth or if expansion occurs while residual remains compressible.
RAHU-2 is challenged if patch accumulation is lower-cost and more predictive than rewrite, or if structural distance cannot distinguish them.
RAHU-3 is challenged if successful adaptive systems preserve invalid authority or authority decay consistently harms long-horizon performance.
Separate corrigibility axis is challenged if capability approximately predicts ACS across sufficiently diverse systems.
Benchmark novelty is challenged if static evaluations reliably predict authority decay, structural updates, and contradiction handling.
Practical relevance of adaptive decoupling is challenged if all tested systems show reality-driven authority revision.
Strongest challenge: fixed-mechanism systems adapting equally well or better would undermine necessity of reality-driven mechanism revision.
Source names wrong attribution, wrong threshold, wrong authority proxy, benchmark overfitting, and missing variables as benchmark failure modes.
RAHU should claim only a measurable property of adaptive systems, not a definition of intelligence.
Each listed 'Result' is a prospective consequence of a falsification condition, not a reported empirical result.
No falsification condition is reported as having been executed or observed on the frozen surface.
Whether ARR tracks causal influence remains an explicitly falsifiable open measurement question.
No validated structural-distance implementation is established by this document.
